candidates: In Storybook story decorators, never execute side effects (e.g. `spyOn`, `mockClear`, global mutations) directly in the decorator function body. Decorator bodies are treated as render-phase code and are invoked twice in React Strict Mode, causing side effects to stack or double-fire. Move all such setup logic into a `useEffect` inside a wrapper component so the side effect runs exactly once after mount.

Do not define React components inside a Storybook decorator body (or any other render function). Inline component definitions create a new function reference on every invocation, causing React to unmount and remount the subtree on each re-render and firing cleanup effects prematurely. Define wrapper components at module scope so their identity is stable across renders.

In client-side manager code, use the shared `logger` from `storybook/internal/client-logger` instead of calling `console.error`, `console.warn`, or other `console.*` methods directly. Direct `console` calls bypass the project's unified logging layer.
